query:
Toronto Hydro has proposed a 2025-2029 custom scorecard with 12 measures. In its
Decision and Order, the OEB set a 2020-2024 custom scorecard with 15 measures.
a) Please confirm, by a list identifying each, which items in the proposed 2025-2029 custom
scorecard are exactly the same measure as the 2020-2024 scorecard measure, without
considering the target itself.
b) Please list and explain the rationale supporting all measures that have the same or similar
name, but Toronto Hydro proposes a different definition of the measure for 2025-2029.
c) For each applicable measure, please explain the rationale supporting the removal of a
2020-2024 scorecard measure from the 2025-2029 scorecard.
For each measure and target on the proposed custom scorecard, please identify which initiatives
would not be pursued in the absence of a performance incentive related to the initiative. For each
such measure, please explain why not.
answer:
**Short answer.** The filings I can access do not contain Toronto Hydro's response to this question set. I found no statement that maps the 12 proposed measures one-for-one against the 2020-2024 measures. I found no measure-by-measure rationale for dropping old measures. I found no statement of which initiatives would not be pursued without a performance incentive. What follows is my own comparison of the evidence, and I flag where it is inference.

One discrepancy first. The 2020-2024 results table lists 16 custom measures, not 15 [cite:rds-823236:274]. A footnote there also says Toronto Hydro "proposed 15 Custom Performance Measures" for 2025-2029, while the scorecard itself has 12 [cite:rds-823236:274] [cite:rds-823236:191]. I could not reconcile these counts, and the Decision's 15 is not in the documents I read.

**The two scorecards**

- **Proposed 2025-2029 (12 measures).** These are Outage Duration (SAIDI), Outage Frequency (SAIFI-Defective Equipment), System Security Enhancements, New Services Connected on Time, Customer Satisfaction, Customer Escalations Resolution, TRIF, Emissions Reductions, ISO Compliance and Certification, Efficiency Achievements, Grid Automation Readiness and System Capacity (Non-Wires) [cite:rds-823236:191].
- **2020-2024 (16 listed).** These are Customers on eBills, TRIF, Network Units Modernization, SAIDI-Defective Equipment, SAIFI-Defective Equipment, FESI-7, FESI-6 Large Customers, MAIFI, System Capacity (# of stations), Wood Poles asset condition, Direct Buried Cable Replacement, In-Service Additions, Average Wood Pole Replacement Cost, Vegetation Management Cost per km, Oil Spills Containing PCBs and Waste Diversion Rate [cite:rds-823236:274].

**a) Same measure, ignoring the target**

- **TRIF** appears to be the only essentially unchanged measure. Toronto Hydro says it "intends to continue reporting TRIF as a custom measure" [cite:rds-823236:276]. The 2020-2024 definition is recordable injuries per 200,000 exposure hours [cite:rds-823236:275]. The new one is injuries per 100 employees (or 200,000 hours) per year [cite:rds-823236:191]. These look equivalent, but the filing does not say so.
- **SAIFI-Defective Equipment** is also the same measure by name and cause-code scope. Toronto Hydro states it "intends to continue reporting on this metric" [cite:rds-823236:279]. The new version is a five-year rolling average with a target range [cite:rds-823236:200]. Whether that counts as a definitional change is a judgment call.

**b) Similar names, different definitions**

- **Outage Duration versus SAIDI-Defective Equipment.**
  - The old measure covered defective-equipment outages only [cite:rds-823236:279].
  - The new measure is total SAIDI excluding Major Event Days (MEDs), Loss of Supply (LoS) and Scheduled Outages. It is stated in minutes on a five-year average [cite:rds-823236:192].
  - Toronto Hydro says it removes the Scheduled Outages cause code for two reasons. One is forecasting uncertainty from the Oracle Utility Analytics implementation. The other is that scheduled outages are expected to rise with a larger work program. It also says the exclusion gives more visibility into unforeseen interruptions [cite:rds-823236:192] [cite:rds-823236:193].
  - It also says the choice reflects customers' priority on shorter outages [cite:rds-823236:193].
  - This is my reading of how the two measures relate: the evidence calls the new measure "custom SAIDI" and it is broader in scope than the old one.
- **Customer Satisfaction versus Customers on eBills.**
  - The 2020-2024 table files eBills under the "Customer Satisfaction" reporting category [cite:rds-823236:274].
  - The proposed Customer Satisfaction measure is a different measure. It uses post-transactional surveys for phone and email inquiries, key accounts, connections, and outage and construction communications [cite:rds-823236:191].
  - Its target is to maintain three-year baselines. Baselines for some areas are still being established [cite:rds-823236:212].
- **New Services Connected on Time.** This is a new composite measure with weights of LV 70%, HV 20% and DER 10% [cite:rds-823236:191]. The Electricity Service Quality Requirements already cover LV and HV connections [cite:rds-823236:292]. The DER component appears new. I did not find a stated rationale for the weighting.

**c) Removed 2020-2024 measures**

The following have no proposed counterpart on the 2025-2029 scorecard. I saw no per-measure rationale for removal:

- Customers on eBills
- Network Units Modernization
- FESI-7
- FESI-6 Large Customers
- MAIFI
- System Capacity (# of stations)
- Wood Poles asset condition
- Direct Buried Cable Replacement
- In-Service Additions
- Average Wood Pole Replacement Cost
- Vegetation Management Cost per km
- Oil Spills Containing PCBs
- Waste Diversion Rate

Several of these are covered by general statements:

- Toronto Hydro says "in place of some of these measures" it proposes the new set [cite:rds-823236:274]. Exhibit 1B, Tab 3, Schedule 2 reports on the old measures as annually reported measures [cite:rds-823236:292].
- On FESI-7 and FESI-6, the evidence says increases are mainly due to better outage data capture from the new Oracle software, not real service decline [cite:rds-823236:281] [cite:rds-823236:282]. It makes a similar caution about MAIFI and SCADA coverage [cite:rds-823236:278]. These explain why those measures are hard to interpret, but the filing does not say they were dropped for that reason.
- The OEB required MAIFI in the last case [cite:rds-823236:277].

**Which initiatives would not be pursued absent an incentive**

The filings available to me do not state this for any measure. The closest evidence is as follows.

- **System Capacity (Non-Wires).**
  - Toronto Hydro plans about $5.7 million for expanded Local Demand Response (LDR) to procure 30 MW, deferring load transfers [cite:rds-823236:230].
  - It says that shared-savings incentives would not "level the playing field" between LDR and conventional load transfers. It also says the proposed incentive (about $3.3 million) is what the filing offers instead [cite:rds-823236:237].
  - It also says distributors "must have appropriate incentives" to build non-wires capability [cite:rds-823236:237].
  - This implies LDR at that scale depends on the incentive. It is not an explicit "would not pursue" statement.
- **Grid Automation Readiness.** It is described as a "least regret" preparation for self-healing grid from 2030 [cite:rds-823236:228]. This is the opposite of an incentive-dependent initiative.
- **Other measures.** The Outage Duration and System Security Enhancements measures are tied to programs funded in the base plan [cite:rds-823236:196] [cite:rds-823236:207]. The evidence also says reliability would deteriorate if funding were cut to IRM levels [cite:rds-823236:195]. That is a funding argument, not an incentive one.
- **How the incentive works.** The incentive works as a $65 million upfront reduction (0.6% X-factor component) that Toronto Hydro can earn back by meeting targets [cite:rds-823236:186]. It is an earn-back of withheld revenue, so the filing frames it as accountability rather than payment for optional work.

**Suggested next step.** Check the interrogatory responses and the OEB Decision itself, which are not among the passages I could retrieve. They are the likely source of the 15-measure count and of any answers on removed measures and incentive dependence.

judge.rationale: The candidate correctly picks out TRIF and SAIFI as carried-over measures. It also gets the SAIDI redefinition right (now excluding MEDs, Loss of Supply and scheduled outages) and gives the customer-priority rationale for it. However, it gives no per-measure removal rationale, so it misses the reference's reasons: eBills target exceeded, the Network Units program winding down, cost measures replaced by Efficiency Achievements, and environmental measures managed under ISO14001. Its suggestion that Local Demand Response depends on the incentive also sits uneasily with the reference, which says the incentive mechanism does not drive any specific initiatives.
